claims.text: Adding 0.1–0.5 wt% carbon to a refractory high-entropy alloy will promote carbide precipitation.
The carbon-induced carbide precipitates will be nanoscale.
The carbon-induced carbide precipitates will be uniformly distributed in the alloy microstructure.
Interstitial carbon atoms will react with refractory-metal components of the alloy to form stable carbides.
The carbide precipitates will impede dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
Impeded dislocation motion from carbide precipitation will enhance high-temperature creep resistance.
Carbon addition at 0.1–0.5 wt% will improve high-temperature strength relative to the carbon-free baseline alloy.
Carbon addition at 0.1–0.5 wt% will improve creep resistance relative to the carbon-free baseline alloy.
The predicted high-temperature improvement will hold at 800–1000°C under sustained-load creep conditions.
Adding 0.1–0.5 wt% carbon will have a negligible or minimal effect on overall alloy density.
Adding 0.1–0.5 wt% carbon will cause little or no decrease in room-temperature tensile strength.
Adding 0.1–0.5 wt% carbon will preserve room-temperature ductility.
The carbon-free refractory high-entropy-alloy baseline has adequate room-temperature properties.
The carbon-free refractory high-entropy-alloy baseline has limited high-temperature mechanical performance.
Carbon contents outside 0.1–0.5 wt% might not produce the anticipated precipitates or might adversely affect other properties.
